title: gpt style model train
text: Simple Local GPT Trainer is a small educational project for local AI experimentation. The project is designed to show how a tiny GPT-style model can be trained from a plain text file. The goal is not to create a powerful language model. The goal is to make the training process easier to see, modify, and understand. A user can place text into the data folder. The preparation script reads the text and trains a small tokenizer. The tokenizer converts text into token IDs. The dataset script splits those token IDs into fixed length training chunks. The training script builds a tiny transformer model from a configuration file. The model learns patterns from the prepared text. The inference script loads the trained model and generates text from a prompt. Small models can learn visible patterns from small datasets. They may also memorize the training text very quickly. This behavior is expected in tiny local experiments. Changing the dataset can change the generated output. Changing the context length can change how much text the model sees at one time. Changing the number of layers can change the size and capacity of the model. Changing the embedding size can strongly affect the parameter count. Changing the tokenizer vocabulary size can affect how text is split into tokens. A tiny model with a tiny dataset may produce repetitive text
